modern: Remember that the ruling faculty is invincible when, collected in itself, it is satisfied with itself, if it does nothing which it does not choose to do, even if it resists out of mere stubbornness. What, then, will it be when it forms a judgement about anything with the help of reason and deliberately? Therefore the mind which is free from passions is a citadel, for man has nothing more secure in which he can take refuge and be impregnable from then on. He, then, who has not seen this is an ignorant man; but he who has seen it and does not take refuge here is unhappy.
original: Remember that the ruling faculty is invincible, when self-collected it is satisfied with itself, if it does nothing which it does not choose to do, even if it resist from mere obstinacy. What then will it be when it forms a judgment about anything aided by reason and deliberately? Therefore the mind which is free from passions is a citadel, for man has nothing more secure to which he can fly for refuge and for the future be inexpugnable. He then who has not seen this is an ignorant man; but he who has seen it and does not fly to this refuge is unhappy.
